summary: Design v2 beats the one-prompt baseline on all three datasets. Held-out test split not run yet.

stages.name: Prove the pipeline
stages.desc: CS and networking short answers: DigiKlausur, SAF, Mohler

stages.name: STEM with working
stages.desc: Maths, physics, chemistry; generated practice sheets, ProcessBench, PRM800K

stages.name: Other fields
stages.desc: Optional, only if a good dataset turns up

steps.name: Set up
steps.note: Project folders, config file, model client with Claude CLI and API backends, 26 tests.

steps.name: Load data
steps.note: DigiKlausur, SAF and Mohler downloaded and loaded into one format; dev/test split by question.

steps.name: Baseline
steps.note: One-prompt grader and metrics script. First number to beat, from 24 DigiKlausur answers.

steps.name: Marking scheme maker
steps.note: Schemes written once per question and self-tested. 8 of 8 passed on DigiKlausur dev.

steps.name: Grader and checks
steps.note: Read-first pass, essence policy, code prices verdicts (partial = 0.9), schemes sized to the model answer. v2b error 0.069 on DigiKlausur seed 0 vs 0.217 baseline.

steps.name: Feedback and its checker
steps.note: Feedback judge run on 2 runs: anchored 96%, names the missed point 100%, actionable 95-100%, but explains why only 33-55%.

steps.name: Readable report page
steps.note: Per-run report.html with equations, numbered reading order, score sum, teacher mark vs ours. Sample view: autograde view --name <run> --limit 10.

steps.name: Improvement loop
steps.note: Batch 1 done (v0 to v2b, see experiments/RESULTS.md). Next: feedback explains why; Mohler still strict.

steps.name: Final held-out run
steps.note: Run once on test questions, then write the results table.

next.t: Run the held-out test split once
next.s: Baseline vs v2b on the test questions of all three datasets. The tuning so far used dev questions only.
Judge shows only 33% to 55% explain why an idea matters. Change the feedback prompt, then rerun the judge.
Bias is still -0.13 there. Look at its biggest gaps in the report page.

next.t: Check robustness to the model answer
next.s: Regrade against a paraphrased and a shortened model answer; report how far marks move.

next.t: Use a judge from a different provider
next.s: Current judge is the same family as the grader, which tends to rate it kindly.

issues.t: Settings were chosen on dev samples
issues.s: Partial weight 0.9 was picked by looking at DigiKlausur seed 1, SAF and Mohler. The test split has not been touched, so treat dev numbers as optimistic.

issues.t: Cost is about 5 times the baseline
issues.s: About $1.0 to $1.3 per 24 answers vs $0.14 to $0.25 at list price (reading, marking and feedback are three calls per answer).
Bias -0.13, error 0.155. Teacher marks there average 4.35 out of 5.

issues.t: Judge shares a model family with the grader
issues.s: Feedback scores are likely a little high.
Only the Claude CLI backend has run.

decisions.t: Fully automatic, no human step at run time
Plain Python, no LangGraph for now
Output format: file per student or table
Git: every GT test is committed and tagged locally
Push to GitHub: manual, when you choose

compare.note: Same 24 answers for both. The settings were tuned on other samples (seed 1, SAF, Mohler), but on the same dev questions. Full history: experiments/RESULTS.md.
